target_customer: Independent auto mechanics and small repair shops in Mexico buying aftermarket parts
problem: Mechanics buy parts through many intermediaries with poor price transparency, uncertain availability and fraud risk. Meru sources directly from manufacturers and bundles purchasing, delivery and financing.
business_model: B2B marketplace take rate on parts sold, plus fintech partner financing
product_category: Auto parts B2B marketplace and supply chain

founders.name: Manuel Rodriguez Dao
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked with the Kavak founding team across growth, data, finance, marketing, sales, business development and IT, and spent 2+ years importing wholesale goods from China to Mexico.

founders.name: Virgile Fiszman
founders.background_notes: YC page: based in Ningbo, China, lived in China 3+ years, focused on international trade.

founders.name: Federico Moscato
founders.background_notes: YC page lists interests in supply chain and logistics.

founders.name: Eduardo Mata
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page and TechCrunch without background.

founders.name: Daniel Ferreyra
founders.background_notes: Named by the TechCrunch Dec 2021 article among the founding team; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Jetz
competitors.what: On-demand marketplace for auto parts aimed at workshops and installers in Mexico City

competitors.name: RIGS
competitors.what: Guadalajara e-commerce startup connecting car owners with auto parts retailers (consumer focus)

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace app plus sourcing, logistics and financing partners. The hard part was operations and China to Mexico supply chain, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships and logistics help, but a competitor could replicate a marketplace; no network effect proven as of founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing incumbents copied or bought the model.

market_need_then: Meru later said each purchase passes through four to five intermediaries and many transactions suffer fraud (company claim, 2026 trade press, unverified). Mexico's aftermarket was fragmented and mechanics had few digital purchasing options.

branding.domain_note: YC lists meru.com. As of 2026 meru.com redirects (301) to getmeru.com, which presents a different product (a dollar account). The auto parts company's current domain was not found.
branding.brand_signature: The company framed itself as the Alibaba of Latin America in TechCrunch coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand-focused coverage found; the name is shared with several unrelated companies such as Meru Networks and Meru Cabs, which hurts search distinctiveness.

outcome_analysis: Meru launched its marketplace in August 2020 and, per TechCrunch, passed 10,000 registered users in about a year with revenue growing 40 to 50 percent monthly, which supported a $15M Series A in December 2021 co-led by Valor Capital and EMLES Ventures. No later round, layoffs or exit was found. YC still lists it as active with about 70 staff, but the meru.com domain now serves an unrelated product, so the current state of the auto parts business is not verified.
notes: PYMNTS corroborates the $15M figure. The earlier round is recorded from a Forbes Mexico article published 2021-03-26: a pre-seed led by Mountain Nazca with angels Ricardo Weder (Justo founder), Roger Laughlin (Kavak co-founder) and David Geisen (Mercado Libre country manager). Its body says 2.3M dollars while its headline and El Referente say 2.4M; 2.3M is used. El Referente returned HTTP 403 and was not opened. This fits the roughly 2M gap between the 17M total and the 15M Series A. Total funding is $17M per TechCrunch; aggregators list other totals (3M, 40M) that conflict. Competitor sources lack dates; Jetz is described as founded 2021. A different Meru (professional services) appears in databases and is not this company. Outcome search found no layoffs or acquisition. Competitors: no dated source near 2021-01 was found. TechCrunch (2022-05-24) names Pandas as doing something similar, but Pandas had operated only about three months then, so it is not added as a competitor at founding. Jetz and RIGS stay undated.
